subject: POC runway: staggered billing + short extension request
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@skyloom.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC runway: request for 3-week runway + blended rate

Hi Sergio —

Thanks again for the demo last week. The team ramped the integration faster than we expected; we’re burning through the token cap and will hit the soft limit by next Tuesday. Our CTO asked if we could get a short extension (3 additional weeks) so we can complete the user-level QA and produce a final evaluation readout.

Budget is tight for this quarter. If you can do a short timebox extension, we’d need a blended discount for the additional runway rather than a full seat uplift — something like 25% off incremental usage for those three weeks. We prefer a single amendment rather than a new contract.

Can you confirm feasibility and what you’d need from us (acceptance, invoice timing)? Also attaching a usage snapshot.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Park
Head of ML Eng, Skyloom

Attachment: usage_snapshot_Mar01.csv (CSV, 14 KB)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@skyloom.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC runway: request for 3-week runway + blended rate

Hi Emily —

Appreciate the quick heads-up and the snapshot — useful. Short answer: likely yes, we can accommodate a 3-week extension with a blended incremental discount, but I need to confirm approval for the 25% number from the finance/ops side.

Next steps from my side: I’ll loop in pricing and legal to draft a one-page amendment (adds three weeks, applies incremental usage discount for the timeframe). For invoicing, we can do a single invoice at the end of the extended period or an immediate pro-rated invoice if you prefer. Which works better for Skyloom?

I’ve copied Laura and Monica to confirm internal approvers and kickoff the amendment draft. I’ll have a proposed amendment back to you by EOD tomorrow if possible.

Best,
Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC runway: request for 3-week runway + blended rate

Sergio / Monica —

I’m fine with a short, time-boxed extension but 25% flat on incremental usage is higher than our standard play for short runway topups. Two possible paths:

1) Approve 25% for incremental usage for 3 weeks, but require a follow-up commitment meeting (no contractual extension beyond the 3 weeks). Finance will want a one-off internal credit approval.

2) Offer a staged discount: 15% on week 1 incremental usage, 20% on week 2, 25% on week 3. The benefit: reduces immediate revenue impact while giving Skyloom a clear runway to finish QA. This also maps to our internal graduated-credit templates and is easier to approve.

If Skyloom prefers invoice timing, push to end-of-term billing (one invoice) to keep collections aligned; otherwise if they want pro-rated now we can do a short-term invoice but that triggers additional billing ops steps.

I’ll prepare a one-page amendment template. Monica, can you run the credit approval?

—Laura
Director, Commercial Operations

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC runway: request for 3-week runway + blended rate

Laura / Sergio —

I ran the numbers. Option 2 (staged discount) is preferable from an ops and revenue-recognition standpoint. It reduces our near-term hit and is easier to reconcile in billing. I can sign off on a staged schedule up to the 25% cap in week 3 given the short duration, assuming Skyloom agrees to a one-page amendment and an end-of-term invoice.

If we go staged, we should also include a cap on incremental usage for the extension period (e.g., no more than 1.5x their current weekly avg) to avoid open-ended spikes. I’ll add suggested lines to the amendment.

Monica
Senior Revenue Operations

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@skyloom.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 16:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC runway: request for 3-week runway + blended rate

Hi Emily —

Thanks for waiting. We can do the short extension under a one-page amendment with the following commercial terms:

- Extension: 3 weeks (Mar 9 – Mar 29)
- Discount schedule on incremental usage above their current baseline: Week 1 = 15%, Week 2 = 20%, Week 3 = 25%
- Cap: incremental usage for the extension period capped at 1.5x weekly avg reported in your snapshot (attachment)
- Invoicing: single invoice at end of extension (Mar 30) for any incremental consumption during the extended weeks
- Acceptance: amendment executed via DocuSign; I’ll attach the draft.

If that aligns, I’ll route the amendment through DocuSign and send over the link. If Skyloom needs a different invoice timing, let me know and I’ll coordinate with finance (Monica).

Best,
Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: POC_Amendment_v2.pdf (PDF, 4 pages)
DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/signon/12345-POC-Amend
